tasks.short: Prepare finance data, run statistical analyses, and interpret results.

steps.what: Agree the finance question, population, period, and intended decision.
Retrieve finance extracts and reconcile source totals.
Inspect missing values, join records, and resolve data quality exceptions.
Choose statistical methods and document assumptions.
Write and execute analysis code, then inspect numerical diagnostics.
Interpret findings and record limitations for finance users.

tasks.design: Configure approved extracts from the {ERP} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with reconciliations and versioned transformation rules. A reusable analysis generator runs tested statistical routines and produces diagnostics; the data scientist resolves exceptions, selects methods, and records interpretation in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance definitions, source mappings, and notebook logic were scattered. Repeating an analysis often required rebuilding its preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors, statistical libraries, and code generation make reusable pipelines cheaper to assemble. Reliable automation still depends on explicit definitions and tested routines.
tasks.still_hard: Missing data, changing account mappings, and causal interpretation require investigation. New questions can fall outside the reusable analysis templates.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a real business effect from an accounting change, selection bias, or unreliable measurement.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rebuilding extracts toward investigating unusual finance movements. A proposed added right is to initiate variance investigations within an agreed scope; financial approval rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Investigate unexplained ledger movements.
reach.learn: Account mappings, posting cut-offs, reconciliation controls, and acceptable adjustment evidence.

evidence.claim: Versioned transformations, reconciliations, and statistical routines can execute deterministically; method choice remains contextual.
Genie supports questions over governed data using trusted assets; this supports prepared access, not unrestricted analytical correctness.
Uber documented faster query drafting while also reporting invented tables; generated queries need validation.

assumptions: The initial scope covers recurring finance analyses with stable source definitions.
Novel methods and unresolved data exceptions return to the data scientist.
Programming and analysis mostly occur in the {DATA_PLATFORM}; document-heavy priors do not imply document-based computation.
Build estimates cover a reusable starter for one finance dataset, not replacement of the data estate.
Access estimates include GDPR review where personal data is involved and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which finance sources, connectors, and reconciliation totals are available.
How much work repeats an existing method versus develops a new one.
Whether personal or employee-level data is included.
Which investigation rights the financial manager would delegate.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the intended use.
research_questions: Which recurring analyses can use existing scheduling and connector configuration?
Do transformations reproduce historical totals across accounting periods?
Which missing-data patterns require investigation rather than an automatic default?
new_work: Review data quality exceptions and failed reconciliations.
Maintain source mappings and approved statistical templates.
Check changes to schemas, definitions, and access permissions.
tasks.statement: Analyze, manipulate, or process large sets of data using statistical software.

tasks.short: Select useful predictors for finance forecasting models.

steps.what: Define the prediction target, forecast horizon, and permitted predictors.
Assemble candidate predictors and check their availability at prediction time.
Run feature selection algorithms within time-aware training and validation splits.
Evaluate performance, leakage, stability, and subgroup differences.
Approve the feature set for the intended model use.
Record approved features, selection settings, and reproducibility details.

tasks.design: A deterministic pipeline on the {DATA_PLATFORM} builds point-in-time datasets from the {ERP} and {CRM}, runs configured selection methods, and generates validation views in the {BI}. Approval in the {WORKFLOW} authorises the feature set for its stated use and generates a reproducible feature record in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selection code was tied to individual notebooks, with inconsistent splits, feature definitions, and experiment records.
tasks.enabler_now: Mature selection algorithms and repeatable experiment pipelines already exist. AI coding makes the surrounding integration and validation harness cheaper to build; no language model is needed for numerical selection.
tasks.still_hard: Point-in-time data, proxy variables, changing business processes, and small samples can invalidate apparently strong results.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a predictor that works in a historical dataset from one that is legitimate and available in practice.

ambition.what: Forecast diagnostics for smaller budget-owning teams

tasks.altitude: The scientist reviews comparable experiments instead of repeatedly wiring selection scripts. They gain capacity to propose model improvements for smaller teams; model approval still requires the designated reviewer.

reach.task: Challenge predictor stability and model limitations.
reach.learn: Model validation standards, proxy risks, and how limitations translate into use restrictions.

evidence.claim: Feature selection, time-aware validation, and reproducibility checks can use ordinary algorithms without a language-model loop.
The digest contains transparent automated statistical modelling products, but no direct finance feature-selection case.
Creditworthiness and life or health insurance pricing can fall within listed high-risk AI uses; classification depends on intended use.

assumptions: The initial use is revenue or cash forecasting, with no automatic decisions about individuals.
A model reviewer may be a senior scientist rather than a separate department.
The means prior overweights documents and meetings for this task; algorithm execution usually happens on the {DATA_PLATFORM}.
The special-category-data prior is not assumed for ordinary finance forecasting.
Numerical execution can largely automate, but target definition and model acceptance retain substantial human judgement.
Build ranges cover a few models on existing infrastructure. GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties must be assessed; employee consultation follows national rules.
unknowns: Whether historical data preserves what was known at each prediction date.
Which models already have repeatable training and validation pipelines.
Whether predictors include personal or special-category data.
Whether intended uses involve creditworthiness, insurance pricing, or employee decisions.
Who has authority to approve features and model use.
research_questions: Which selection methods remain stable under realistic temporal validation and changing finance conditions?
Which leakage checks can be automated, and which require business review?
What computation budget gives useful comparisons without excessive search?
new_work: Review leakage warnings and unstable predictor rankings.
Maintain approved predictor definitions and temporal joins.
Monitor performance and relevant subgroup differences.
Retest the pipeline when source schemas or business processes change.
tasks.statement: Apply feature selection algorithms to models predicting outcomes of interest, such as sales, attrition, and healthcare use.

tasks.short: Choose survey populations and produce defensible samples or complete population lists.

steps.what: Agree survey objectives, population boundaries and required precision.
Assemble and reconcile the eligible population from source records.
Choose sampling or enumeration, strata and nonresponse assumptions.
Calculate sample sizes and allocations using statistical code.
Draw a reproducible sample or produce the complete eligible population list.
Approve coverage, selection integrity and the roster's release for survey preparation.

tasks.design: A deterministic pipeline in {DATA_PLATFORM} builds a permissioned population frame from the required {ERP} or {HCM} records and flags coverage gaps. The scientist specifies the design; tested formula code calculates allocation and produces a reproducible sample or complete roster with a selection log. A release control in {WORKFLOW} exposes the roster only after the scientist approves it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Population definitions and source identifiers varied between surveys. Frame cleaning and selection records were often rebuilt for each exercise.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable frame checks, explicit design forms and tested sampling code can now be assembled with less development effort. No model loop is needed once the scientist supplies the design.
tasks.still_hard: Missing populations, nonresponse bias and small subgroups can invalidate nominal precision. GDPR limits roster access and retention; employee surveys may require consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether the population frame and response assumptions support the conclusion the finance team wants to draw.

ambition.what: Sampling support for smaller cost-centre teams previously omitted from finance planning surveys.

tasks.altitude: The scientist spends less time assembling lists and more time checking coverage and precision. Method and roster approval remain with the scientist; no new authority to contact people is assumed.

reach.task: Design a sample for a finance control test.
reach.learn: Audit objectives, tolerable error and why survey precision differs from audit assurance.

reach.task: Estimate cost drivers from a representative internal survey.
reach.learn: Cost-centre structure and how missing responses affect forecast assumptions.

evidence.claim: Explicit sampling designs, formula-based allocation and seeded selection can use deterministic code.
The PowerGPT evaluation separates model-assisted test selection from statistical-engine computation; its clinical results do not validate this survey workflow.
Population coverage and nonresponse assumptions require judgement despite automated sample selection.

assumptions: The example is an internal finance cost-driver survey; only necessary source records are used.
Population and design inputs are entered explicitly rather than inferred from prose.
Existing statistical code is reused where it has suitable checks.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates; consultation elapsed time can exceed working effort.
unknowns: Which records define the eligible population and who may access them.
Whether stable identifiers and subgroup attributes exist.
Required precision, response rates and acceptable disclosure thresholds.
Applicable national consultation rules and existing employee agreements.
Whether smaller teams can be included without exposing individual responses.
research_questions: How much undercoverage exists when the source frame is compared with an independent population count?
Which proposed subgroup estimates remain useful under realistic nonresponse?
new_work: Resolve missing or conflicting population records.
Maintain sampling formulas and reproducibility checks.
Review coverage, response assumptions and roster releases.
Remove expired rosters and audit access.
tasks.statement: Apply sampling techniques to determine groups to be surveyed or use complete enumeration methods.

tasks.short: Clean finance data, resolve ambiguous records and publish validated datasets for analysis.

steps.what: Retrieve raw finance extracts and record their reporting periods.
Profile missing values, duplicates, formats and distributions in a statistical programming environment.
Resolve ambiguous entries with the finance data owner.
Decide mapping, exclusion, imputation and adjustment rules for analytical use.
Apply cleaning rules in a statistical programming environment and inspect changed records.
Reconcile totals, review exclusions and approve the analytical dataset.
Publish the approved dataset and document its lineage and limitations.

tasks.design: A versioned pipeline on the {DATA_PLATFORM} retrieves extracts from the {ERP}, profiles them and applies approved cleaning rules to a separate analytical copy. Reconciliation results appear in the {BI}, and an approval in the {WORKFLOW} releases the dataset with generated lineage notes in the {DOCS}. Unexpected schema changes or failed controls stop publication and enter an exception queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exports changed, cleaning decisions were buried in scripts, and source meanings were undocumented. Automating an unclear correction would only repeat the ambiguity faster.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connectors, validation rules and reusable transformation components. Structured finance data usually needs deterministic checks rather than a language model.
tasks.still_hard: Missing values, inconsistent accounting meanings and late adjustments require source-owner judgement. GDPR purpose limits, retention and access controls must also hold for derived datasets.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an erroneous entry from a legitimate financial exception, and preserve information that matters to the analysis.

ambition.what: A reconciled receivables analysis dataset released after each weekly refresh.

tasks.altitude: The scientist spends less time rerunning cleaning scripts and more time resolving source meaning and testing analytical sensitivity. Publication remains an approval right within the analytical environment; correcting the financial ledger remains with the authorised finance role.

reach.task: Investigate recurring reconciliation differences at their source.
reach.learn: Learn posting cut-offs, reversals, currency handling and which corrections require an accounting entry.

evidence.claim: Structured profiling, transformations, control-total reconciliation and lineage generation can use deterministic code.
The digest recommends integrations and configured edit checks for data preparation. Its clinical examples are adjacent patterns, not finance deployment evidence.
GDPR obligations continue to apply to personal data in analytical copies and derived datasets.

assumptions: The pilot covers recurring extracts from a small number of finance sources.
The current statistical programming environment is represented by {OTHER}.
Approved cleaning rules cover repeat transformations; novel mappings and material rule changes require human decisions.
Raw extracts remain unchanged, and analytical transformations never write back to the ledger.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates.
The access range includes applicable employee consultation under national rules; no contested employee-monitoring rollout is assumed.
unknowns: Which extracts, volumes and refresh frequencies are involved?
Are stable identifiers, source control totals and historical snapshots available?
Who can explain source anomalies and approve material cleaning decisions?
What personal data, retention requirements and access restrictions apply?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the intended dataset?
research_questions: Which historical cleaning decisions can become explicit, tested rules?
Which reconciliation failures indicate extraction problems rather than legitimate adjustments?
What should block publication, and what can be released with a documented limitation?
new_work: Review publication controls and unresolved data exceptions.
Maintain mappings, schema contracts and reconciliation tolerances.
Add tested transformation components when approved rules change.
Monitor access, retention and recurring source-quality problems.
tasks.statement: Clean and manipulate raw data using statistical software.

tasks.short: Compare finance models using reproducible statistical metrics, business costs and robustness checks.

steps.what: Choose evaluation metrics, holdout periods, comparison groups and financial error costs.
Load frozen outcomes and model predictions into a statistical programming environment.
Calculate metrics, uncertainty, baseline comparisons and segment results in a statistical programming environment.
Copy metric results into a comparison workbook.
Interpret robustness, leakage risks and financial trade-offs before selecting a preferred model.
Record the comparison, selected model version and reasons for the choice.

tasks.design: A configured job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} freezes evaluation inputs and runs versioned scoring code against an approved protocol. Results feed the {BI} directly, eliminating the comparison workbook, while a deterministic generator records the scientist's selection and rationale in the {DOCS}. Selecting a preferred model does not deploy it or authorise its use in individual decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metrics were already computable, but model outputs, holdout definitions and financial cost assumptions differed between runs. Manual comparison workbooks obscured reproducibility.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes reusable evaluation harnesses and report generators cheaper to assemble. The statistical calculations remain deterministic and testable.
tasks.still_hard: Leakage, changing populations and an unsuitable loss function can make precise scores misleading. Creditworthiness uses require separate regulatory classification and validation.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a defensible evaluation design and recognise when an apparent improvement will fail under real financial conditions.

ambition.what: Weekly challenger review for the cash-receipts forecast.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer repeated scoring runs and workbook updates, leaving more time for temporal validation and error analysis. The scientist can recommend a challenger more frequently; production promotion rights do not change.

reach.task: Challenge whether a model comparison is adequate for its intended financial use.
reach.learn: Learn validation independence, materiality thresholds, stress scenarios and evidence required for model approval.

evidence.claim: Statistical metrics, resampling, baseline comparisons and report generation can run as deterministic code.
The PowerGPT trial separated model-assisted test selection from computation by a statistical engine. It supports that architectural separation, not finance model validation.
The digest identifies creditworthiness assessment as an EU AI Act high-risk use; actual classification depends on intended use and applicable exceptions.

assumptions: The pilot compares existing models; training new models and production deployment are separate work.
The current statistical programming environment is represented by {OTHER}.
Existing compute and storage are available in the {DATA_PLATFORM}.
The future review consumes direct results from the {BI}, replacing the comparison workbook.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates.
No new individual employee monitoring is introduced; applicable national consultation must be assessed if that scope changes.
unknowns: Which models, datasets and business decisions are in scope?
Are outcomes mature enough to provide reliable holdout labels?
Who approves metrics and financial error costs?
Are model runs and source snapshots reproducible today?
Is independent validation required before any model use?
research_questions: Do current rankings change when temporal splits and financial costs are held constant?
Which checks detect leakage and missing prediction rows before scoring?
What compute budget and evaluation cadence are appropriate?
new_work: Maintain metric definitions, baseline cases and scoring tests.
Investigate failed runs and mismatched prediction identifiers.
Review changes to holdout periods, population coverage and cost assumptions.
Maintain evaluation lineage and dependency versions.
tasks.statement: Compare models using statistical performance metrics, such as loss functions or proportion of explained variance.

tasks.short: Turn analysis results into clear, accurate finance visualizations.

steps.what: Clarify the audience, decision, measures, and comparison period.
Aggregate results and prepare chart measures and comparison groups.
Choose chart forms, scales, comparisons, and uncertainty displays.
Build charts, labels, filters, and page layouts.
Check figures, readability, accessibility, and potentially misleading visual choices.
Publish the approved view and set internal access.

tasks.design: Prepare reconciled chart datasets in the {DATA_PLATFORM} and configure reusable chart templates in the {BI}. Automated checks compare displayed measures with source results; reviewed views publish to an approved audience, while scheduled refreshes use the same tested definitions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts were rebuilt for each request, with inconsistent measure definitions and formatting. Existing visualization features still needed someone to prepare trustworthy inputs.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable semantic measures, chart templates, and automated rendering checks reduce assembly work. A language model is unnecessary for routine chart production.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing comparisons and communicating uncertainty remain contextual. Small groups, unusual distributions, and unfamiliar audiences need additional care.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when an accurate chart invites the wrong conclusion and redesign it around the actual decision.

ambition.what: Accessible budget variance views for department budget holders.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer formatting requests and more work testing whether people understand the charts. A proposed added right is to select visual standards for approved finance measures; publication and data-access authority remain subject to existing delegation.

reach.task: Maintain a certified finance reporting model.
reach.learn: Measure definitions, access rules, accessibility checks, and refresh dependencies.

reach.task: Explain departmental budget variances.
reach.learn: Which comparisons lead to useful budget actions and which need accounting context.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports generated report pages on prepared semantic models; model preparation and review remain necessary.
Chart generation, scheduled refreshes, and numerical comparison checks can use configured software and deterministic code.
Clear visual comparisons, uncertainty displays, and accessibility require evaluation beyond checking numerical accuracy.

assumptions: The {BI} supports reusable templates, controlled access, and scheduled refreshes.
The initial scope uses approved finance measures and internal audiences.
Most assembly can be automated, while chart choice and final review retain human time.
Build estimates include access review and any applicable employee consultation under national rules.
GDPR applies where views contain personal data; employee-level monitoring requires separate assessment.
unknowns: Which measures already have agreed definitions.
Whether current {BI} permissions match the proposed audiences.
Whether charts expose small groups or individual staff performance.
Which accessibility requirements and visual standards are already adopted.
research_questions: Can configured chart templates cover the recurring visualization requests?
Do users correctly interpret uncertainty and comparison periods in sample views?
Can automated checks detect stale data, broken filters, and incorrect displayed totals?
new_work: Review new chart specifications and material changes.
Maintain templates, certified measures, and audience permissions.
Handle refresh failures and collect comprehension feedback.
tasks.statement: Create graphs, charts, or other visualizations to convey the results of data analysis using specialized software.

tasks.short: Explain analytical findings, answer finance questions, and record agreed decisions.

steps.what: Clarify the management decision, audience, and questions to address.
Assemble approved charts, figures, definitions, and limitations.
Draft the presentation narrative, implications, and speaker notes.

loop.input: Presentation brief and approved evidence pack with stable figure and chart references.
loop.output: Draft narrative and speaker notes with evidence references for substantive claims.
loop.check: Resolve every numerical reference against the evidence pack; flag unsupported claims for human review.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved claims remain flagged and the scientist completes them.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble figures but cannot adapt explanations and caveats to varied management questions.

steps.what: Verify claims, recommendations, uncertainty, and suitability for the audience.
Share the approved presentation with the intended internal audience.
Present findings, answer challenges, and discuss decision options.
Record agreed decisions, unresolved questions, owners, and due dates.

loop.input: Written discussion notes identifying explicitly agreed decisions and actions.
loop.output: Draft decision record and action list, with missing owners or dates marked.
loop.check: Each entry links to a note passage; the scientist confirms agreement, owners, and dates before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous entries return to manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes vary in wording; extraction helps without requiring recording or autonomous follow-up.

tasks.design: An evidence-linked generator assembles approved outputs from the {BI} and {DOCS}, then a bounded model loop drafts audience-specific explanations. The data scientist approves the pack before configured internal distribution through the {EMAIL}, leads the discussion, and reviews extracted decisions before they enter the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Presentation preparation mixed mechanical copying with audience-specific explanation. Generic templates could assemble slides but could not reliably express nuanced findings.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured evidence packs and bounded drafting make preparation easier to automate. They do not establish whether a recommendation is sound or secure stakeholder agreement.
tasks.still_hard: Live challenges, conflicting incentives, sensitive conclusions, and ambiguity about agreed actions require a person. Clear prose can still overstate weak evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, explain uncertainty under challenge, and help decision makers confront uncomfortable trade-offs.

ambition.what: Short finance decision clinics for department budget holders.

tasks.altitude: Preparation takes less of the week, leaving time for smaller decision discussions and follow-up questions. Presentation support does not confer authority to commit budgets or make management decisions.

reach.task: Frame a finance decision and compare feasible responses.
reach.learn: Decision thresholds, budget authority, timing constraints, and the evidence needed to act.

reach.task: Explain forecast changes to budget holders.
reach.learn: How to translate uncertainty into practical planning choices.

evidence.claim: Novo Nordisk documented drafting reports from approved text with human review; the vendor case supports assisted drafting, not equivalent finance savings.
Evidence-linked templates can assemble figures deterministically while a bounded model drafts explanatory text.
Live interpretation, stakeholder advice, and acceptance of recommendations require contextual human judgement.

assumptions: The baseline audience is internal management and finance users.
Approved numerical outputs exist before presentation drafting starts.
The model receives only data approved for its processing environment.
Decision extraction uses written notes; meeting recording is outside the initial scope.
Build estimates include access and confidentiality review, GDPR assessment where needed, and consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which presentation formats and evidence repositories are used.
Who may approve and distribute sensitive finance findings.
Whether an approved model-processing environment is available.
Whether management decisions require confirmation by a different role.
Whether budget holders want and can attend the proposed decision clinics.
research_questions: Can numerical claims be inserted as verified references rather than generated values?
How often do drafts omit caveats or turn associations into causal claims?
Can decision extraction distinguish proposals from explicitly agreed actions?
new_work: Review narratives, caveats, and evidence references.
Maintain presentation templates and drafting evaluation examples.
Resolve ambiguous decisions and missing action owners.
Check distribution permissions when audiences change.
tasks.statement: Deliver oral or written presentations of the results of mathematical modeling and data analysis to management or other end users.

tasks.short: Design and test surveys that collect useful finance planning data.

steps.what: Agree the decisions, measures and respondent burden the survey must address.
Draft questions, response scales and routing in a document.

loop.input: Measurement brief, approved question library and instrument schema.
loop.output: Draft questionnaire with scales, routing and links to intended measures.
loop.check: Validate schema and routing; the scientist checks neutrality, construct coverage and unnecessary personal questions.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions; unresolved measurement issues return to the scientist.
loop.why_not_simpler: New finance concepts need wording adapted to respondents; established items are reused directly.

steps.what: Review measurement quality, privacy, accessibility and respondent burden.
Build the survey form and test routing, validation and export fields.
Complete a supervised pilot and explain confusing questions.
Revise the instrument and document its measures and coding.
Approve the instrument for distribution after required reviews are complete.

tasks.design: A versioned question library in {DOCS} supplies established items, while a bounded loop drafts only the wording needed for new measures. Configured forms in {WORKFLOW} implement routing and validation, and deterministic generators produce the data dictionary and test report. The scientist reviews measurement quality and pilot feedback before a separate release approval; invitations remain a downstream action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Question wording, form configuration and coding documents were maintained separately. Automating form creation did little to solve unclear measures or misunderstood questions.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured instrument definitions can drive forms, tests and documentation together. A bounded drafting loop can suggest wording while keeping established questions and human pilot testing.
tasks.still_hard: Neutral wording, valid measures, translation and credible anonymity remain difficult. GDPR requires an appropriate basis, minimisation and retention controls; employee surveys may need consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Notice what respondents misunderstand or hesitate to disclose, and decide whether a question should be asked at all.

ambition.what: A short cost-driver pulse survey that supplements quarterly finance forecasts.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to form setup and duplicate documentation; more goes to pilot interviews and measurement quality. The scientist retains instrument design responsibility, while the finance manager retains release approval.

reach.task: Collect explanations for changing cost and demand assumptions.
reach.learn: Which respondent answers can support a forecast adjustment.

reach.task: Review employee survey collection and disclosure arrangements.
reach.learn: Purpose limits, retention, anonymity and applicable national consultation requirements.

evidence.claim: Configured forms can implement routing and validation; a shared instrument schema can generate coding documentation.
Question drafting can be assisted, but the digest provides no direct case establishing survey validity from generated wording.
Human pilot interviews help identify misunderstood concepts and response burden.
For the Netherlands, the digest identifies works-council consent requirements for specified individual staff-performance systems; applicability depends on the survey's use.

assumptions: The survey collects internal cost-driver information rather than individual performance ratings.
The existing form capability supports routing, access controls and structured export.
Pilot participation and review remain human activities.
Time shares include participant and approver effort, not only the scientist's time.
Build ranges cover one instrument family; consultation and pilot scheduling can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Available form features and approved question libraries.
Respondent groups, languages and accessibility needs.
Who approves measurement quality, privacy arrangements and release.
Applicable national consultation obligations.
Whether responses can be anonymous and whether linkage is necessary.
research_questions: Do respondents interpret generated questions as the measurement brief intends?
Can one instrument definition reliably generate forms, routing tests and the data dictionary?
Does a short pulse survey improve forecast decisions enough to justify respondent effort?
new_work: Review new wording and maintain approved question versions.
Run pilot interviews and resolve ambiguous questions.
Maintain routing tests and export mappings.
Manage retention, access and release records.
Monitor respondent burden and survey fatigue.
tasks.statement: Design surveys, opinion polls, or other instruments to collect data.

tasks.short: Identify finance problems that analysis can address and agree useful, feasible questions.

steps.what: Read incoming requests and extract the reported problem, requester and desired outcome.

loop.input: An analysis request and its directly linked attachments.
loop.output: Structured request summary with quoted evidence and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate the schema and source references; absent facts remain blank.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; ambiguous requests enter the clarification queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing requests arrive as varied free text. A structured form can replace this loop for new submissions.

steps.what: Review financial trends and exceptions for problems worth investigating.
Clarify the stakeholder's decision, constraints, current response and definition of success.
Inspect source coverage, history, permitted access and available outcome labels.
Judge whether analysis can support an actionable decision with the available evidence.
Write the analytical question, success measure, exclusions and proposed first test.

loop.input: Confirmed requirements, feasibility judgement and a fixed problem-brief template.
loop.output: Draft problem brief with a measurable question and explicit exclusions.
loop.check: The data scientist checks actionability, outcome definitions and consistency with the feasibility judgement.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved definitions return to stakeholder clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: The structure is fixed, but the problem statement must synthesise context-specific requirements.

steps.what: Agree the priority, sponsor and allocation of analytical capacity.

tasks.design: A structured intake form in the {WORKFLOW} captures new requests, while a bounded extraction loop converts existing messages from the {EMAIL} and {CHAT}. Configured exceptions in the {BI} and deterministic profiles on the {DATA_PLATFORM} support stakeholder discovery. A brief generator prepares the scoped question in the {DOCS}, and approved priorities enter the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests lacked common fields, and discovering whether usable data existed required repeated investigation. The business decision often remained implicit.
tasks.enabler_now: Small intake applications and metadata checks are cheaper to build. Bounded extraction can organise existing requests while structured forms reduce future extraction work.
tasks.still_hard: Available data does not establish causality or make a question useful. GDPR purpose limits and national rules can restrict proposed uses of personal or employee data.
tasks.human_edge: Find the decision behind a vague request and recognise when a process change would help more than another model.

ambition.what: A monthly analytical scoping clinic for budget owners without dedicated analyst support.

tasks.altitude: The data scientist spends less time reconstructing requests and checking basic source coverage. A proposed decision right is to return incomplete requests or offer a small diagnostic within a capacity allowance; portfolio priority remains with the finance manager.

reach.task: Turn a recurring budget variance into a testable management question.
reach.learn: Learn the budgeting calendar, controllable cost drivers and which responses a budget owner can actually take.

evidence.claim: Genie uses curated assets and example queries to support questions over governed data; this supports prepared evidence access, not autonomous problem selection.
Structured intake, source profiling and rule-based exception lists can automate preparation for analytical scoping.
Whether a question is actionable depends on stakeholder constraints and analytical judgement.

assumptions: The automate classification is a prior; the decomposition retains human discovery, feasibility judgement and prioritisation.
Configured exception lists identify candidates, not confirmed business problems.
The pilot covers a small set of recurring finance sources.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates.
The access range includes applicable employee consultation under national rules for the limited pilot; contested monitoring proposals fall outside it.
unknowns: Which request channels and existing intake forms are used?
Is source metadata available and current?
Who may prioritise or reject analytical requests?
Would the proposed questions involve employee monitoring or new uses of personal data?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: How often do recent requests lack a decision owner, success measure or actionable response?
Which feasibility checks can be answered reliably from metadata?
Does a structured form reduce clarification without discouraging useful requests?
new_work: Review incomplete or incorrectly extracted requests.
Maintain intake fields and source metadata checks.
Tune exception thresholds to avoid an unmanageable candidate list.
Review whether prioritised work produced useful decisions.
tasks.statement: Identify business problems or management objectives that can be addressed through data analysis.

tasks.short: Find finance trends, relationships, and factors that could distort analysis.

steps.what: Frame hypotheses and identify business changes that might affect results.
Retrieve finance data and inspect missing values, definitions, and coverage.
Calculate trends, relationships, and subgroup summaries; produce exploratory charts.
Investigate confounding, seasonality, outliers, and alternative explanations.
Write findings with uncertainty, limitations, and supporting charts.

loop.input: Validated exploration and sensitivity results, chart references, and scientist-written interpretation notes.
loop.output: Findings draft distinguishing observed associations from supported causal conclusions.
loop.check: Populate figures deterministically; trace claims to results; flag unsupported causal language for scientist review.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims are omitted or marked; manual writing is the fallback.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed chart captions are easy, but connecting case-specific findings and caveats needs prose.

steps.what: Challenge the findings and approve their release to finance stakeholders.

tasks.design: Reusable jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} retrieve {ERP} and {CRM} data, run quality checks, and produce exploration and sensitivity artefacts. A bounded loop drafts findings in the {DOCS} from validated results, while an analysis reviewer approves release and approved trends can feed the {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exploration was bespoke, business change notes were separate from data, and analysts repeatedly assembled the same checks and charts.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable statistical code and data contracts can standardise the repeatable work. AI coding lowers the cost of packaging these checks, while a bounded loop can draft supported explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Confounding, changing definitions, selective exploration, and missing business context remain difficult to resolve.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an appealing relationship is an artefact and decide what evidence would change the conclusion.
tasks.altitude: The scientist spends more of the week investigating surprising changes and testing explanations. They can propose follow-up investigations, while approval of released findings remains explicit.

reach.task: Explain changes in revenue and margin.
reach.learn: Accounting effects, operational drivers, and which explanations are material to finance decisions.

reach.task: Maintain recurring trend reports.
reach.learn: Certified measure definitions, refresh schedules, and how to distinguish monitoring from exploratory analysis.

evidence.claim: Prepared reporting models support assisted questions and report creation; unprepared models can produce misleading answers.
A documented company implementation reduced query-writing time but still encountered invented tables.
Exploration and sensitivity calculations can be automated, while interpreting confounding requires domain and statistical judgement.

assumptions: The starting dataset concerns finance performance rather than clinical research.
Exploratory findings are labelled separately from confirmatory results.
The priors correctly emphasise judgement, but overstate document and meeting time for hands-on exploration.
High apparent automation potential does not remove the need to investigate alternative explanations.
Build ranges cover one recurring dataset and a limited exploration library.
GDPR applies where data identifies people. Employee performance reporting may require consultation or consent under national rules.
unknowns: Which source definitions changed during the analysis period.
Whether business change notes are available and reliable.
Who independently reviews findings before release.
Whether datasets or dashboards reveal individual employee performance.
research_questions: Which sensitivity checks should run by default for the recurring finance questions?
How should exploratory comparisons be recorded to expose selective reporting?
How reliably can draft checks identify unsupported causal claims?
new_work: Triage data quality and trend alerts.
Maintain statistical checks and business change annotations.
Review draft findings and claim-to-result links.
Investigate false alarms and revise monitoring thresholds.
tasks.statement: Identify relationships and trends or any factors that could affect the results of research.

tasks.short: Use analysis to recommend solutions to finance problems.

steps.what: Clarify the finance question, constraints, and decision owner.
Retrieve analysis results and reconcile them with current finance figures.
Calculate financial scenarios using agreed assumptions.
Assess trade-offs and choose a recommendation.
Write a decision brief explaining benefits, uncertainty, and alternatives.

loop.input: Proposed recommendation, validated scenario results, assumptions, and decision brief template.
loop.output: Draft decision brief with links to supporting figures.
loop.check: Insert numbers deterministically; check each factual claim against supplied evidence; scientist reviews interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence stays marked; failed checks return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover the structure, but explanations of case-specific trade-offs need prose.

steps.what: Discuss the brief and approve, reject, or revise the recommendation.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles approved analysis results with {ERP} actuals and feeds a scenario calculator in the {BI}. A template generator creates a decision brief in the {DOCS}, with a bounded loop drafting explanations; the financial manager approves the recommendation before budget changes proceed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Financial definitions, scenario assumptions, and decision context were scattered across reports, workbooks, and conversations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing data interfaces and calculation libraries support reusable scenario tools. AI coding can reduce implementation effort, while bounded drafting can use approved figures.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing defensible assumptions, recognising causal limits, and balancing competing business interests remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Understand why a financially attractive option may fail operationally and challenge the decision owner's assumptions.
tasks.altitude: The scientist spends less time rebuilding scenario workbooks and more time challenging assumptions with finance leaders. They can propose weekly intervention reviews; spending authority remains with the financial manager.

reach.task: Prepare driver-based budget scenarios.
reach.learn: Budget ownership, driver definitions, and how approved scenarios become forecast revisions.

evidence.claim: Prepared semantic models support assisted finance reporting and report drafting, but require reliable definitions.
A documented vendor case reports fewer manual analysis tickets; this supports faster access, not automated business judgement.
Deterministic scenario calculators and template-based decision briefs are feasible; proposed time shares and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: A recurring budgeting or working-capital question provides the initial scope.
Scenario assumptions remain explicit and versioned.
The meeting share follows the priors; more analytical work occurs in systems than their means split suggests.
Build ranges cover one reusable workflow using existing infrastructure, not a company-wide finance transformation.
GDPR applies to personal data, and EU AI Act obligations depend on the use case. National rules may require employee consultation.
unknowns: Which finance measures are approved and who maintains them.
Whether current finance actuals and analysis results have accessible interfaces.
Who approves budget changes and working-capital interventions.
Whether scenarios use employee-level data or require employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which reconciliation checks reliably detect stale or inconsistent finance figures?
How much preparation time does the scenario tool save without increasing decision errors?
new_work: Review drafted explanations and unresolved evidence gaps.
Maintain scenario assumptions and finance mappings.
Investigate reconciliation failures and stale data.
Record whether approved recommendations achieved their expected effects.
tasks.statement: Identify solutions to business problems, such as budgeting, staffing, and marketing decisions, using the results of data analysis.

tasks.short: Propose mathematical solutions to finance forecasting, allocation and risk problems.

steps.what: Agree the finance decision, constraints and success measures.
Extract finance data and reconcile it to agreed control totals.
Select mathematical methods and define assumptions and benchmarks.
Code models, run scenarios and compare results against benchmarks.
Interpret results and write a solution proposal with limitations.

loop.input: Validated results, approved assumptions, limitations and a proposal template.
loop.output: Draft solution proposal with links to calculated results.
loop.check: Numbers are inserted deterministically; the scientist checks interpretation, uncertainty and recommendations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported explanations return to the scientist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining tradeoffs for a specific decision requires prose beyond fixed result tables.

steps.what: Review tradeoffs and approve a pilot or request changes.

tasks.design: A reusable project template in {WORKFLOW} connects an analysis brief to reconciled {ERP} data in {DATA_PLATFORM}. Versioned deterministic models generate scenarios, validation reports and {BI} views; a bounded loop drafts the proposal from verified results. The scientist approves its interpretation, and the finance manager separately approves the pilot.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance definitions, extraction code and validation routines differed between projects. Reusable components took time to build, while method choice remained specific to each problem.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can make reusable connectors, scenario runners and test harnesses cheaper to build. Established numerical methods still perform the calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Causal assumptions, leakage, changing business conditions and poorly specified objectives remain difficult. Creditworthiness uses involving natural persons can trigger EU AI Act high-risk requirements; GDPR applies when personal data is processed.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a defensible objective and explain why a mathematically strong result may be a poor finance decision.

ambition.what: A finance scenario clinic that compares cash, cost and service tradeoffs before pilot approval.

tasks.altitude: The scientist spends more of the week comparing assumptions and advising decision owners. Finance retains pilot and spending approval; any delegated experiment budget needs an explicit mandate.

reach.task: Compare budget scenarios under uncertain demand.
reach.learn: Budget ownership, forecast drivers and acceptable planning tolerances.

reach.task: Choose which analytics pilot deserves funding.
reach.learn: Investment hurdles, operational constraints and decision deadlines.

evidence.claim: Versioned numerical pipelines can calculate scenarios and validate results without a runtime model loop.
Copilot in Power BI supports report creation and semantic-model questions; this does not establish reliable mathematical method selection.
Uber documents faster query drafting alongside invented-table errors, supporting schema checks before execution.
EU AI Act Annex III includes specified creditworthiness uses involving natural persons.

assumptions: The initial scope covers recurring finance analysis patterns, not arbitrary new mathematical research.
Calculations use deterministic numerical code with reviewed specifications.
AI-assisted development is distinct from runtime automation.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one reusable analysis pattern.
unknowns: Available data interfaces and reconciliation controls.
How many past projects share a useful analysis pattern.
Whether proposed uses affect natural-person creditworthiness or other regulated decisions.
Personal data, permitted purposes and approved processing arrangements.
Who can approve pilots and experimental spending.
research_questions: Which repeated analysis pattern has stable definitions and a trustworthy baseline?
Can generated proposals preserve uncertainty without overstating recommendations?
new_work: Maintain reusable model templates and numerical tests.
Investigate reconciliation failures and unexpected scenario results.
Review drafted interpretations and limitations.
Monitor deployed models for changing data and business conditions.
tasks.statement: Propose solutions in engineering, the sciences, and other fields using mathematical theories and techniques.

tasks.short: Read research and assess emerging methods for finance analytics.

steps.what: Define research topics from current finance analytics problems.
Search research indexes and save relevant papers.
Read papers and record methods, findings, limitations and supporting passages.

loop.input: Accessible papers and a fixed research-note schema.
loop.output: Research notes with page references, quotations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check references against source text; the scientist reads important passages and methods.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per paper; unreadable or unsupported content returns to the scientist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Methods and limitations appear in varied prose, equations and tables.

steps.what: Judge research quality and relevance to available finance data.
Write a short research brief with suggested experiments.

loop.input: Reviewed research notes, method shortlist and a brief template.
loop.output: Trend brief with attributed claims and proposed experiments.
loop.check: Each factual claim links to reviewed notes; the scientist checks recommendations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims are omitted or marked for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: A useful synthesis connects findings across papers in plain language.

steps.what: Share the approved brief with finance analytics colleagues.

tasks.design: Configure alerts in research indexes under {OTHER} and deduplicate accessible papers into {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop creates cited notes, and a drafting loop uses reviewed notes to prepare briefs. The scientist judges applicability and approves each brief before {WORKFLOW} distributes its link through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research alerts already existed. Reading varied papers and connecting findings to local finance problems still required substantial attention.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded text extraction can prepare traceable notes. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting alerts, document templates and review queues.
tasks.still_hard: Technical validity, publication bias, inaccessible papers and transfer to local finance data still require careful reading.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an attractive result depends on assumptions that fail in the company's finance setting.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one finance analytics method for a small feasibility check.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to searching and first-pass notes; more goes to reproducing promising results. The scientist can recommend experiments more often, but gains no automatic spending or deployment authority.

reach.task: Assess a proposed risk-monitoring method.
reach.learn: Risk assumptions, validation standards and the cost of false alerts.

evidence.claim: Alerts, deduplication and document templates can handle collection and distribution; research appraisal remains judgement-heavy.
Cited extraction and drafting are plausible assistance, but the digest provides no documented research-reading case.
EU AI Act Article 4 requires AI literacy for relevant staff using AI systems.

assumptions: The scientist follows public research relevant to finance forecasting, risk or operations.
Research notes form most of the work; correspondence is a small share.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The first version uses public papers and excludes confidential finance data from model inputs.
unknowns: Available research subscriptions and permitted automated access.
Approved model-processing arrangements and document retention rules.
Whether a weekly experiment shortlist would help the finance team.
Existing alert and document-review features.
research_questions: Can reviewers verify extracted limitations faster than writing notes themselves?
Which research sources provide reliable metadata and accessible full text?
new_work: Check citations and omitted limitations.
Maintain research topics and source filters.
Handle inaccessible papers and extraction failures.
Refresh a small benchmark of papers with known findings.
tasks.statement: Read scientific articles, conference papers, or other sources of research to identify emerging analytic trends and technologies.

tasks.short: Recommend analytical solutions to finance stakeholders and explain their costs, benefits and uncertainty.

steps.what: Gather financial measures, model results and the agreed business question.
Calculate financial scenarios and compare expected benefits, costs and uncertainty.
Write a recommendation explaining the evidence, alternatives, limitations and proposed action.

loop.input: Approved decision evidence, calculated scenarios, business constraints and recommendation template.
loop.output: Draft recommendation with alternatives, source references and explicit uncertainty.
loop.check: Numbers are inserted from calculations. The data scientist checks interpretation, causal claims and recommendation suitability.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or unresolved contradictions return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template fills figures, but explaining trade-offs requires contextual language.

steps.what: Discuss the recommendation, challenge assumptions and negotiate practical trade-offs.
Approve, reject or defer the proposed business action.
Record the decision, action owner and follow-up date.

tasks.design: A reusable calculation service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles approved evidence and produces scenario comparisons for the {BI}. A bounded drafting loop prepares a brief in the {DOCS}, which the data scientist approves before discussion. The finance manager records the business decision through the {WORKFLOW}, which creates follow-up actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence, assumptions and narrative were assembled separately. Reusable decision templates and consistent financial measures were often missing.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building calculation and document generators. Bounded drafting can explain verified figures without calculating them.
tasks.still_hard: A predictive improvement may have little business value. Causal uncertainty, implementation capacity and conflicting incentives still require discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the evidence supports a narrower claim, and help stakeholders accept the associated trade-offs.

ambition.what: Monthly review of which overdue-invoice segments should receive a collections experiment.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling recommendation packs toward testing assumptions and discussing interventions. A proposed additional right is to commission small sensitivity analyses within an agreed scope; spending and operational changes remain with the finance manager.

reach.task: Choose a suitable collections intervention for an overdue-invoice segment.
reach.learn: Understand contact constraints, payment disputes and how collectors judge whether an intervention is workable.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI supports questions and report generation over prepared semantic models; this supports evidence preparation.
Novo Nordisk used model drafting from approved text for clinical reports. This is an adjacent drafting case, not evidence of finance recommendation quality.
Scenario calculations, decision records and source-linked briefs can be implemented with deterministic software.

assumptions: The pilot covers one recurring finance decision with agreed measures and accessible evidence.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates, not measured outcomes.
Stakeholder discussion remains substantial despite the opportunity to automate preparation.
The access range assumes no new individual employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which recurring decision has a clear owner and measurable financial outcome?
Are scenario assumptions and financial measures already agreed?
What authority can the data scientist exercise without additional approval?
Do the evidence sources contain personal data or employee-level measures?

Can each material claim be traced to an approved measure or documented assumption?
Does the generated brief improve decision clarity during a trial with stakeholders?
new_work: Review generated interpretations and source references.
Maintain scenario assumptions and calculation tests.
Resolve contradictory evidence and unsupported recommendations.
Check outcomes against the recorded decision assumptions.
tasks.statement: Recommend data-driven solutions to key stakeholders.

tasks.short: Backtest finance models, investigate failures, and approve justified revisions.

steps.what: Define outcomes, validation periods, benchmarks, and acceptance criteria.
Freeze data versions and construct time-aware training and validation splits.
Run backtests, benchmarks, calibration checks, and relevant segment tests.
Investigate errors, leakage, instability, and business significance.
Revise features, assumptions, or model structure.
Repeat validation and compile the candidate comparison and limitations.
Review validation evidence and accept, reject, or request further work.
Register the approved version for the internal forecast process.

tasks.design: Build a versioned validation harness in the {DATA_PLATFORM} with frozen splits, benchmark comparisons, leakage checks, and reproducible report generation. The data scientist investigates failures and designs revisions; the {WORKFLOW} permits registration of a forecast model only after the financial manager records approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Validation code and evidence were rebuilt across models. Acceptance criteria and business costs were often implicit.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable testing components and faster code assembly reduce validation plumbing. Statistical validity and model reformulation still require expertise; training a predictive model does not require an autonomous language-model agent.
tasks.still_hard: Structural economic changes, rare outcomes, feedback effects, and unavailable future labels limit validation. A better historical score may fail to improve the finance decision.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when the target, assumptions, or business use is wrong despite apparently strong test results.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward investigating model failure and comparing justified alternatives. The scientist could gain authority to initiate recalibration reviews; approval to use a revised finance model remains with the designated approver.

reach.task: Challenge model assumptions and assess model limitations.
reach.learn: Independent validation, materiality, stress scenarios, and evidence needed for acceptance.

reach.task: Translate forecast errors into planning adjustments.
reach.learn: Planning horizons, asymmetric error costs, and actionable forecast tolerances.

evidence.claim: Backtests, fixed data splits, benchmark comparisons, and report tables can run deterministically after expert specification.
The PowerGPT trial separated model-assisted test selection from statistical-engine computation; its results do not establish autonomous finance model validation.
EU AI Act Annex III includes specified creditworthiness and life or health insurance pricing uses; intended use must be assessed.

assumptions: The baseline use is internal financial forecasting, hence the plan-to-forecast workflow.
The current process includes a financial manager approving business use; specialist independent validation may also be required.
Revisions return to investigation when validation fails; test sets are protected against repeated tuning.
Historical outcomes and reproducible model execution are available.
Build estimates include GDPR and EU AI Act use-case assessment, access, and applicable consultation under national rules.
Judgement-heavy reformulation keeps substantial human time despite the task's automation prior.
unknowns: Which model purposes, outcome labels, and forecast horizons apply.
Whether models affect creditworthiness, insurance pricing, employment, or other regulated decisions.
Who currently approves model use and whether independent validation is required.
Whether historical data can be reconstructed as it was known at each forecast date.
Which compute capacity and version controls are available.
research_questions: Do historical splits prevent temporal and entity leakage?
How stable are candidate rankings across periods, segments, and plausible stress conditions?
Which acceptance criteria reflect the cost of forecast error?
Can existing model registration and approval features cover the release controls?
new_work: Maintain benchmarks, validation datasets, and acceptance criteria.
Investigate failed tests, changing error patterns, and outcome-label delays.
Review release evidence and preserve rejected candidate histories.
Monitor approved models and schedule reassessment.
tasks.statement: Test, validate, and reformulate models to ensure accurate prediction of outcomes of interest.

tasks.short: Write and maintain functions or applications for finance analysis.

steps.what: Define analytical behaviour, interfaces, and acceptance criteria.
Inspect existing functions, schemas, and reusable analysis components.
Write analysis functions and applications in the script editor.

loop.input: Approved specification, selected existing code, schemas, and reusable function templates.
loop.output: Proposed code patch and relevant test cases.
loop.check: Check syntax, interfaces, dependency policy, and independent acceptance examples; scientist inspects analytical logic.
loop.stop: One patch and two revisions within the specified files; unresolved requirements return to the scientist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard functions; novel analytical requirements need code synthesis.

steps.what: Run numerical, edge-case, integration, and performance checks.
Diagnose failures and revise the analysis code.

loop.input: Failing test evidence, relevant code, acceptance criteria, and permitted change scope.
loop.output: Proposed corrective patch with an explanation tied to the failure.
loop.check: Rerun independent tests; reject changes that weaken checks or alter the specification; scientist reviews the diagnosis.
loop.stop: At most two patch-and-test cycles with a ten-minute execution budget; unresolved failures return to manual diagnosis.
loop.why_not_simpler: Format and syntax fixes are deterministic; semantic failures require interpreting code and test evidence.

steps.what: Review analytical correctness and approve the code for release.
Release approved code to the internal analysis environment and record its version.

tasks.design: A code generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines reusable templates with bounded drafting and repair loops driven by specifications in the {DOCS}. Configured checks run in an isolated environment, and release automation publishes only the exact code version approved by the reviewer, recording the outcome in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Analysis requirements varied, reusable code was hard to discover, and reliable tests and release paths were uneven.
tasks.enabler_now: Code generation can produce reviewable patches from specifications and examples. Existing test runners and release controls bound the work; no autonomous agent is needed.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible implementation can silently use the wrong statistical method, mishandle missing values, or pass inadequate tests.
tasks.human_edge: Specify the analytical meaning, design independent checks, and recognise correct-looking code that answers the wrong question.
tasks.altitude: The scientist spends less time on boilerplate and more time specifying behaviour and reviewing numerical correctness. They can propose shared component interfaces; release approval remains with the code reviewer.

reach.task: Turn validated analysis components into recurring reports.
reach.learn: Report interfaces, refresh reliability, and how component changes affect certified measures.

reach.task: Reproduce and inspect calculation controls.
reach.learn: Reconciliation evidence, audit trails, and accounting tolerances for automated calculations.

evidence.claim: A documented text-to-SQL implementation shows faster code drafting with remaining hallucination risks; it does not establish general application-writing performance.
Trusted SQL assets and examples can constrain assisted query generation.
Bounded code drafting, independent tests, human review, and version-controlled release are feasible; these build and time estimates are unvalidated.

assumptions: An existing internal code environment supports versioning, test execution, and controlled release.
Generated code uses synthetic or approved test data and cannot access production credentials.
Release automation verifies that the approved version and released version are identical.
The means prior substantially overweights documents and meetings for programming; most execution occurs on the {DATA_PLATFORM}.
The owner's 10-to-100-times build-speed bet is a hypothesis, not an evidenced delivery guarantee.
Build ranges cover a generator for a narrow component family, not arbitrary application development.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations remain relevant to generated applications; employee consultation depends on national rules and intended use.
unknowns: Which code, test, and release facilities already exist.
Whether code may be processed by an approved model service.
Which independent reference calculations and acceptance examples are available.
Who reviews code and approves internal releases.
Whether the target applications influence decisions about individuals.

How often do generated patches pass independent numerical checks and human review?
What measured implementation gain remains after integration, review, and rework?

Maintain templates, permitted dependencies, and independent reference tests.
Handle failures beyond the bounded repair budget.
Monitor released components and maintain rollback versions.
